result.topic_en: Euler lists the successive space-derivatives of the deflection of a vibrating elastic rod, then (Corollary 3) gives the velocity and acceleration of a point of the rod with respect to time, and begins a scholium noting the infinite variety of regular vibratory motions arising from the arbitrary constants.

items.english: From these formulas it is seen how all the prescribed conditions are satisfied.

items.quote: tamen ob ingentem quantitatum conſtantium arbitrariarum numerum infinita varietas locum habere poteſt, prouti iſtae conſtantes aliter atque aliter determinantur.
items.english: Yet because of the great number of arbitrary constants an infinite variety can occur, according as these constants are determined in one way or another.
